passages.text: “Possessions, honor, and popularity are grim, bitter, and harsh. They’re an obstacle to reaching the supreme sanctuary from the yoke. So you should train like this: ‘We will give up arisen possessions, honor, and popularity, and we won’t let them occupy our minds.’ That’s how you should train.”
passages.note: Not letting status and popularity take over the mind

passages.text: “Whether they’re honored or not honored, or both, their immersion doesn’t waver as they abide in the immeasurables. They persistently meditate with subtle view and discernment. Rejoicing in the ending of grasping, they’re said to be a true person.”
passages.note: Staying steady whether praised or ignored
